questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I did not want to go on exchange if it meant great compromises to my academic furthering. I chose to study abroad at NYU because this would let me see and live in the great city of New York while studying at a university with high academic standards when it came to mathematics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As a private university, NYU was great at providing personal assistance when one did not know what to do and where to find the necessary information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, NYU was great at providing personal assistance. They almost always returned calls and e-mails immediately.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: This is not to say that it was easy to sign up for courses or knowing exactly what to do when if you had trouble understanding the VISA process, but the service provided by NYU in connection hereto was on another level.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not easy to find housing in New York. I highly reccomend applying for housing at Bikubenfonden where I was lucky to secure a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think the experience as a graduate student at NYU is different to what one would expect at most other programs and institutions in New York. The campus at NYU is part of the urban city (kind of like it is in Copenhagen). Therefore, a unifying campus did not really exists, and so living off campus did not mean that one missed out on a whole lot I think. Also, I do not think it is common to live in a dorm on campus as a graduate student in the US in general.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was ofcourse quite complicated to apply for a visa, get the right vaccinations (or documents saying that you did not need them) and so on. No amount of help changes this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NYU was really helpful and personalized help was almost always available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I took all the courses that I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write your professors! This is apparently common practice in the US.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level seemed to be lower at NYU (i.e. the easy courses were really easy), but one was able to take courses as difficult or even more difficult than at UCPH. I also did a research project at NYU, and I think that my supervisor allocated more time to helping me with this than would be expected in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The reading was more extensive. Even in the easy courses, the material was greater than in Denmark. It took a little while to get used to reading more and learning less.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Probability Theory II
Machine Learning
Independent Study

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Do a research project/independent study if you can!
Also, the one course I took at the Data Science master (Machine Learning) was not quite at the standards expected at UCPH.

questions.answer: Food is super expensive in New York. Shop at local food stands if available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure. I don't think many master's students pursued many non-academic opportunities at NYU.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go see New York I guess.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Aside from all the things to see in New York, I highly recommend taking a trip to Washington D.C.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: This was not that difficult. Americans are very friendly and open-minded.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To be honest, it is way easier to be a stranger in the U.S. compared to Denmark. People a friendly and helpful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fact that Americans are so open-minded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Start the process well in advance (most important are the language tests and the visa application).
Apply for housing through Bikubenfonden (at the Academic Guest House in New York).
Write your professors.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are under 26, you can book quite nice tickets to New York through the SAS Young program.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning new mathematics.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning new mathematics.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
